questions.q: What does sign 135 warn of?
options: A total ban on pedestrians in this stretch of road
A place where no vehicle may stop
A pedestrian crossing nearby; be ready to stop
A pedestrian traffic light ahead
questions.explain: Sign 135 is a warning sign: a pedestrian crossing is nearby, and you must slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.q: You are approaching a pedestrian crossing, and a vehicle in the next lane has stopped right before the crossing. What should you do?
options: Hoot so the vehicle that stopped moves on
Overtake the stopped vehicle on its left
Continue driving normally because your lane is clear
Slow down and, if necessary, stop too, because a pedestrian may be crossing and hidden from you
questions.explain: If a vehicle in the next lane has stopped before a pedestrian crossing, you must slow down and, if necessary, stop too — it may be hiding a crossing pedestrian from you (reg. 67(a2)).

questions.q: Which of the following counts as a pedestrian, under the law's definition?
options: Also someone pushing a pram or wheelchair, or wheeling a bicycle by hand
Only someone inside a marked pedestrian crossing
Only a child under 12
Only someone walking on foot with nothing else
questions.explain: The definition of a pedestrian (reg. 1) also includes someone pushing a pram, an invalid carriage or a wheelchair, and also someone wheeling a bicycle along the road (reg. 133).

questions.q: A driver did not let a pedestrian complete a crossing safely at a pedestrian crossing. What is the penalty?
options: {{fine:pedestrian-crossing-entry}} only, with no points
Immediate licence disqualification
{{fine:pedestrian-crossing}} and {{points:pedestrian-crossing}} points
A verbal warning only, with no fine
questions.explain: Not letting a pedestrian complete a crossing safely at a pedestrian crossing: {{fine:pedestrian-crossing}} and {{points:pedestrian-crossing}} points (reg. 67(a)).

questions.q: There is no pedestrian crossing, subway or footbridge nearby, but there is a junction close by. Where must a pedestrian cross the carriageway?
options: They must wait for a vehicle to stop for them voluntarily
Only where there is street lighting
Anywhere convenient, as long as they look before crossing
Near the junction
questions.explain: When there is no pedestrian crossing, subway or footbridge nearby, but there is a junction close by — the pedestrian crosses near the junction (reg. 110(c)).

questions.q: You are approaching a group of children playing at the roadside. What is the legal duty?
options: Hoot continuously so they move away
Speed up to pass them as fast as possible
Slow down
There is no special duty beyond ordinary driving
questions.explain: Near a group of children you must slow down, and stop if necessary (reg. 52(5)).

questions.q: A bus carrying children, marked as such, has stopped at the roadside to pick up children. What should you do as you pass it?
options: Continue at your usual speed, because the bus stopped, not you
Slow down significantly and be ready to stop
Hoot to warn the children
Overtake it quickly on its right
questions.explain: When approaching a vehicle carrying children, marked as such, that has stopped to pick up or drop off children, and as you pass it — you must slow down (reg. 52(13)).

questions.q: An elderly person is crossing a pedestrian crossing more slowly than usual, and a few seconds have already passed. What should you do?
options: Wait for them to complete the crossing — the duty to allow a safe crossing is not limited in time
Creep forward slowly behind them to save time
Hoot to hurry them along
Overtake them within the crossing
questions.explain: The duty to let a pedestrian complete a crossing safely (reg. 67(a)) is not limited in time; if the crossing takes longer, you wait.

questions.q: Who is a “disabled person” for the purposes of the law, in relation to using the road?
options: Anyone over the age of 60
Only someone with a disabled badge on the windscreen
Someone a doctor has recognised as needing a vehicle for mobility because of a physical disability
Only someone riding a mobility scooter
questions.explain: A disabled person, for the purposes of the law, is someone a doctor has recognised as needing a vehicle for mobility because of a physical disability, and who is granted accommodations because of this.

questions.q: There is a marked cycle path beside the carriageway. Where must the cyclist ride?
options: Wherever they choose, as long as they do not obstruct traffic
On the carriageway, because it is faster
On the pavement
On the marked cycle path
questions.explain: Where a marked cycle path has been provided, the cyclist must ride on it and not on any other part of the road (reg. 129(b)).

questions.q: What is the minimum age for riding a bicycle on a non-urban road?
options: There is no age limit
{{fact:bike.nonurban_min_age}}
questions.explain: The law forbids anyone under {{fact:bike.nonurban_min_age}} from riding a bicycle on a non-urban road (reg. 129(f)).

questions.q: Who must wear a protective helmet when riding an e-bike?
options: Only someone riding on a non-urban road
Only minors
Every rider, at all times and on every road
Only someone riding above 20 km/h
questions.explain: When riding an e-bike, a protective helmet is compulsory for every rider, at all times (reg. 39P(a)(4)) — unlike an ordinary bicycle, where the duty depends on age and road type.

questions.q: You are getting out of your vehicle parked at the roadside in the city, beside a cycle lane. What should you do before opening the door?
options: There is no special duty; cyclists are responsible for being careful
Look behind you and make sure no cyclist is approaching
Only open the rear door
Open it quickly so as not to hold up traffic
questions.explain: You must not open a vehicle door until every precaution needed for the safety of road users has been taken (reg. 80(a)); suddenly opening a door in front of an approaching cyclist is a common and preventable injury.

questions.q: When is it allowed to overtake a cyclist even near a junction, where overtaking an ordinary vehicle is forbidden?
options: When the overtaking meets all the other overtaking rules — a clear road and no risk
Never — the ban applies to overtaking a bicycle too
Only if the cyclist signals that they agree
Only during daylight hours
questions.explain: The law exempts overtaking animals, bicycles and an animal-drawn vehicle from the ban on overtaking near a junction, provided the overtaking meets the other overtaking rules — a clear road at a sufficient distance and without risk (reg. 47(f)(2)).

questions.q: What is the minimum age for riding an electric (kick) scooter?
options: There is no minimum age, only a height limit
{{fact:escooter.min_age}}
questions.explain: Minimum age for riding an electric scooter: {{fact:escooter.min_age}} (reg. 122A(a)).

questions.q: There is no marked cycle path on this stretch of road. Where may you ride an electric scooter?
options: On the carriageway
Only on the shoulder
On the pavement, carefully
You may not ride an electric scooter at all without a cycle path
questions.explain: You may ride an electric scooter on a marked cycle path, or, where there is none, on the carriageway; riding on the pavement is forbidden (reg. 122A(b)).

questions.q: An electric scooter rider carried an extra passenger behind them. What is correct?
options: Allowed, as long as the passenger wears a helmet
Forbidden, and this offence carries {{fine:ebike-passenger}}
Up to two extra passengers are allowed
Allowed only for children
questions.explain: Carrying an extra passenger on an electric scooter is forbidden (reg. 122B(c)); the offence carries a fine of {{fine:ebike-passenger}}.

questions.q: What is a “mobility scooter”, and how should a vehicle driver expect it to behave?
options: A small motorcycle that drives on the carriageway like an ordinary vehicle
A type of e-bike
A vehicle for people with limited mobility, that travels mainly on the pavement and enters the carriageway only to cross it
A small utility vehicle for cleaning streets
questions.explain: A mobility scooter is an electric vehicle for people with limited mobility, its speed limited to {{fact:speed.mobility_scooter}}, and it enters the carriageway only to cross it (reg. 39K).

questions.q: Why is it easy to miss an approaching motorcycle in the mirror?
options: Because motorcycles always travel too fast to be seen
Because motorcycles have no duty to use lights by day
Because the law exempts motorcyclists from using turn signals
Because its narrow width makes it easy to disappear into the blind spot, and its speed is hard to judge
questions.explain: A narrow motorcycle easily disappears into the blind spot and barely fills the mirror; its speed is also hard to judge with a quick glance — so before changing lane you must turn your head and check directly.

questions.q: Before turning left at a junction against oncoming traffic, what is the safe rule of thumb regarding motorcycles?
options: Look once and decide quickly
Turn only if there is a green light, with no need for another look
Turn immediately if you do not see anything big approaching
Look twice — the second glance sometimes reveals a motorcycle missed by the first
questions.explain: A quick glance checks whether there is anything big; a second glance sometimes reveals a small motorcycle that was missed by the first. You must not turn based on a guess about the distance of an approaching motorcycle.

questions.q: You are driving behind a motorcycle. Why should you keep a bigger margin than behind a car?
options: Because a motorcycle has no brake lights
Because a motorcycle can stop in a very short distance, and is more sensitive to potholes and oil on the road
Because motorcycles always travel too slowly
There is no special reason; the margin is the same for every vehicle
questions.explain: A motorcycle can stop in a very short distance, and is more sensitive than a car to potholes, loose gravel, oil and a side wind — so it requires a bigger margin.

questions.q: You are in a stationary traffic jam and want to shift lane slightly. What is especially important to check?
options: The blind spot — a motorcycle may be moving between the lanes where a moment ago there was nothing
Only the lane you came from
Only the rear-view mirror
There is no need to check anything, because the traffic is stationary
questions.explain: In traffic jams a motorcycle may filter between lanes or ride alongside a line of stationary cars; you must check the mirror and the blind spot before any movement, even a small one.

questions.q: An animal is crossing the road ahead of you. What is the legal duty?
options: Hoot continuously until it moves
Speed up to get past it
There is no special duty beyond ordinary driving
Slow down, and stop if necessary
questions.explain: A driver must slow down, and stop if necessary, when meeting or overtaking animals on the road (reg. 52(11)).

questions.q: What does sign 146 warn of?
options: Animals may cross or be present on the road
A pedestrian crossing for cyclists
A traffic-calming area
No entry for a works vehicle
questions.explain: Sign 146 is a warning sign: animals may cross or be present on the road ahead of you.

questions.q: A large animal, such as a horse or a cow, is standing on the road ahead of you. What is the safe action?
options: Swerve sharply to avoid hitting it, even if that means crossing into the oncoming lane
Hoot continuously until it leaves the road
Brake in a straight line without swerving sharply
Speed up to get past before it moves
questions.explain: Facing a large animal, you brake in a straight line; a sharp swerve to avoid hitting it can cause loss of control or a head-on collision — more dangerous than the impact itself.

questions.q: When is it allowed to lead a camel train on the road?
options: Only at night, so as not to disrupt traffic
Only when they are tied to one another in a single line, in groups of up to five
Leading camels on the road is forbidden under any circumstances
Without restriction, as long as there is one handler
questions.explain: A camel train is allowed only when the camels are tied to one another in a single line, in groups of up to five (reg. 139).
